We will visit the Parque Lezama, talk about the former Palacio Lezama, and the Museo Histórico Nacional. We also see the monument to Argentine-Uruguayan friendship and the monument to Pedro de Mendoza, the founder of the city. We then walk along Calle Defensa to Plaza Dorrego, known for its antiques and tango. We visit the colonial house \"Solar de French\" and the church Nuestra Señora de Belén, where I tell you about Pedro González Telmo - the patron saint of sailors and the namesake of the district. Finally, we will explore the Mercado de San Telmo with its special flair. The tour is in German - ideal for anyone who wants to experience history in a lively way!
evidence.title: City Tour Through San Telmo

evidence.snippet: San Telmo is the oldest neighbourhood in Buenos Aires, and its cobblestone streets hold enough history to fill several lifetimes. On this self-guided walking tour, you'll trace how sailors, slaves, immigrants, and tango singers turned a muddy colonial outpost into the soul of the city. You'll also discover how a yellow fever epidemic, two British invasions, and millions of Italian immigrants each left their mark on this single neighbourhood. The tour starts at Basílica de San Francisco, where a time capsule is hidden inside a stone statue on the facade. From there, you'll walk south along Defensa Street, passing the oldest pharmacy in Buenos Aires and the spot where residents repelled two British invasions from rooftops using stones and boiling water. You'll also hear how that resistance helped spark Argentina's independence movement, and why the street you're walking is named after those events.

Characterized by narrow cobblestone streets, 19th-century mansions, and rich tango heritage, a historical walking tour through San Telmo uncovers the dramatic evolution of Buenos Aires from a muddy 16th-century outpost to a bustling cosmopolitan hub.
